description: VerdeAI is built by a team of five, led by team owner Arissa. Together with Raden, Amirah, Iffat and Hakim, the team is bringing NASA Earth data, local crop knowledge and a simple website into one tool that helps Malaysian farmers decide what to plant next.
summary:
Every farmer knows the feeling of looking out over their fields and wondering what to plant next. Weather is harder to predict, and soil weakens when the same crops grow season after season. VerdeAI was built to make that decision simpler. Farmers sign up, mark their farm on a map, and tell us about their land: its size, soil type, fertilizers, water sources, current crops and priorities. VerdeAI then uses NASA Earth observation data on rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and crop health to understand real conditions on the farm and combines it with local knowledge of Malaysian crops. In return, farmers get a clear comparison of at least three crop rotation options, including what they do today. Each option comes with a plain explanation, the evidence behind it and the risks worth checking. A simple dashboard shows weather trends, pest and water supply risks, and the best time to switch crops.
VerdeAI is here to support farmers when they decide.
details:
VerdeAI is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make more informed decisions about crop selection, farming practices, and environmental conditions. By integrating NASA Earth observation data, weather information, geospatial mapping, and artificial intelligence, VerdeAI transforms complex environmental datasets into accessible insights that support more sustainable agricultural decision-making. The platform uses the NASA POWER API to retrieve historical climate and agricultural-related environmental data, including temperature, rainfall, humidity, evaporation, and solar radiation. It also integrates NASA MODIS satellite data through NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), allowing users to explore MODIS Terra true-colour satellite imagery alongside vegetation indices, particularly the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), to assess vegetation conditions and monitor changes in plant health. OpenStreetMap provides the base map tiles, which are combined with the GIBS satellite imagery and vegetation layers to create a more informative geographical view of agricultural areas. In addition, the Open-Meteo API provides weather forecasts, precipitation predictions, and terrain elevation data for environmental and terrain analysis, while the Groq API powers an AI agricultural assistant that provides crop-related information, guidance, and recommendations. When satellite data is unavailable, the prototype uses estimated fallback values, which are treated as approximations rather than actual satellite observations. By bringing these different sources of information together in one interactive platform, VerdeAI aims to make agricultural data easier to understand and use, helping farmers examine climate patterns, monitor vegetation conditions, and consider environmental factors when planning their farming activities. The project offers potential benefits such as improved access to agricultural information, greater awareness of changing climate conditions, more informed crop-related decisions, and support for sustainable farming practices. Its intended long-term impact is to contribute to more climate-resilient agriculture, responsible resource management, and healthier farming systems. What makes VerdeAI creative is its combination of publicly available NASA Earth observation data, geospatial mapping, weather services, and AI technology to address a practical agricultural challenge, transforming raw scientific information into a more accessible and interactive decision-support experience. Throughout development, the team considered important factors such as climate conditions, vegetation health, terrain characteristics, crop requirements, data availability and reliability, user accessibility, environmental sustainability, and technical feasibility. VerdeAI was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, and Express.js, with Visual Studio Code as the primary development environment, Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration, and Render for web deployment. Ultimately, VerdeAI demonstrates how space-based data and modern digital technologies can be applied to support smarter agricultural decisions and encourage a more sustainable future for farming.
